Hi Olivia — great to hear you're ready to move ahead. Below is a concise plan we use for Hosted->Dedicated migrations; I'll tailor the numbers after a quick sizing validation run. Proposed timeline:

1) Sizing validation run (3 days) — Redwood will run a staged load against a Dedicated staging pool that mirrors your planned production config. We measure token/sec, 50/95/99 latencies, KV cache hit rate, and model-quality smoke checks.
2) Canary cutover (8–12 hours) — gradual traffic shift (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with health gates.
3) Acceptance window (24 hours) — final SLA verification and handoff to Acme SRE.

Immediate next steps I propose:
- Schedule a 60-minute sizing call tomorrow where we walk through token profiles and peak patterns.
- Redwood to run two synthetic validation passes: one simulating burst traffic and one sustained throughput run.
- Define acceptance gates: 99th latency <250ms, error rate <0.5%, KV cache hit >=65% for prefix-heavy traffic.

I've attached a Mutual Action Plan template you can share with contracts. I'll include an internal sizing calc and ask Marcus for GPU mix suggestions.

Available slots: 2027-06-29 10:00-11:00 PT or 2027-06-29 15:00-16:00 PT. Which works for your team?

Best,
Nikhil Sharma

Team — forwarding Olivia's traffic profile. Quick run-through of our preliminary sizing thoughts so we can agree on a staging config for the validation run: 

Assumptions (from Acme):
- Sustained average: 1.6M tokens/min (~26.6k tokens/sec)
- Burst (95th percentile): ~4x sustained for ~30–90s windows
- Model: redwood-7b-q4 (kv cache applicable for chat threads)

Initial calc (back-of-envelope):
- Kernel performance for 7b-q4 on A100: ~120 tokens/sec per GPU for real workloads (with batching).
- For sustained 26.6k tokens/sec -> ~222 GPUs (unbatched) but with batching, caching, and sharding we typically see 6–8x efficiency.
- Estimate: 28–40 A100-equivalent GPUs to hit sustained. Allow 2.5x headroom for bursts and canary failover -> target pool: 70 GPUs worth of capacity.

Questions for Marcus:
- Can we draft a staging GPU mix that matches this capacity but with a realistic catalog (H100, A100, A10 options)?
- What's the recommended batch sizing and KV cache policy for a 99th <250ms goal?

I'll bake these numbers into the validation run and include a CSV of the calc. Attaching quick calc sheet.

Thanks — read the calc. A few adjustments and a concrete staging mix below: 

1) GPU mix recommendation for staging (mirror of prod):
   - 6x H100 80GB (model serving leaders for large sequence perf)
   - 20x A100 80GB (bulk token throughput)
   - 6x A10 (low-cost embedding/encoder workers)
   - Total "A100-equivalent" ~= 42 units with patch-level kernel tuning (we use a weighting factor of 0.9 for H100->A100 equivalent due to perf differences).

2) Batching & KV cache: aim for adaptive batching target 64 tokens/batch for chat (lower for very short chats) and aggressive KV prefix caching for threads with repeat context. We should aim for >=70% KV hit during the sustained run — that gets us closer to the lower GPU count in the calc.

3) Burst handling and fallbacks: configure smart-routing with a cost-tier fallback to smaller quantized variants; fallback pool capacity = 30% of planned to keep 95th under control while preserving 99th for core customers. Also suggest a quick autoscale window (30–60s) to absorb 2–3x short bursts.

4) Canary plan: 4-stage ramp (internal smoke -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automated rollback on gate failure (latency/error thresholds).

I can run a quick kernel tuning pass on our side and produce a staging config that maps to the numbers above. Do we want to include an on-prem-style network test (latency + MTU) in the staging run? Could be helpful if Acme's SRE expects identical network characteristics.

— Marcus
